title: Lost in the Middle Mitigation
summary: Test and reduce position-sensitive evidence loss in long prompts through selection, ordering, local extraction, and explicit coverage checks.
overview: Lost in the middle describes a research-observed tendency for some models and tasks to use information less reliably when it appears deep inside long contexts. The effect depends on model, task, evidence density, and prompt construction. It should be treated as an evaluation risk, not a universal claim that every model always ignores its middle tokens.

Mitigation begins with reducing irrelevant context, then testing evidence placement. Useful strategies include ranking important passages early, keeping the current question clear, extracting local facts before synthesis, and checking coverage of required evidence. Duplicating every important fact at both ends can waste tokens and create conflicting copies when revisions change.

production.poc: A prototype moves the same supporting passage among several prompt positions and compares answer correctness.
production.production: Production adds position-variation tests, evidence selection, source-aware ordering, and a check for missing required facts.
production.scale: At scale, repeat evaluation after model or template changes and measure effects across document length, language, and multi-source reasoning tasks.

components.name: Position-sensitive evaluation set
components.role: Holds evidence constant while varying its placement and surrounding distractors.

components.name: Evidence selector
components.role: Removes irrelevant or redundant passages before ordering.

components.name: Context organizer
components.role: Places high-value evidence and clear task instructions deliberately.

components.name: Local extraction stage
components.role: Extracts supported facts from bounded sections when full-context synthesis is unreliable.

components.name: Coverage validator
components.role: Checks whether all required evidence dimensions appear in the final answer.

flow.title: Establish positional baseline
flow.description: Evaluate identical questions with supporting evidence near the beginning, middle, and end.

flow.title: Reduce distractors
flow.description: Remove passages that do not support a required answer dimension.

flow.title: Order with provenance
flow.description: Group coherent sources and place critical evidence according to measured model behavior.

flow.title: Extract locally if needed
flow.description: Produce cited section-level facts before combining them into a larger synthesis.

flow.title: Validate coverage
flow.description: Check missing constraints, exceptions, and source conflicts rather than answer fluency alone.

flow.title: Re-evaluate changes
flow.description: Repeat positional tests after changing the model, context budget, or assembly template.

useCase.title: Reviewing a long supplier agreement
useCase.situation: A procurement assistant compares obligations across a lengthy agreement and several schedules.
useCase.problem: An exception located in the middle of the assembled context is repeatedly omitted from summaries.
useCase.requirement: Preserve the exception and show its source alongside the general obligation.
useCase.architecture: The pipeline selects relevant sections, extracts local obligation facts, and validates a coverage matrix before synthesis.
runtime: The agreement’s general clause and schedule exception are extracted separately with citations.
The final comparison checks that both facts appear and that their relationship is explained.
useCase.failure: If a model upgrade regresses middle-position tests, the rollout remains on the previous evaluated configuration.
useCase.impact: Measure exception coverage and positional sensitivity alongside context cost; adding more context can worsen the evidence-to-distractor ratio.

tradeoffs.benefit: Can improve access to important passages.
tradeoffs.cost: Benefits vary by model and task.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces the burden of one large synthesis.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds calls and can lose cross-section relationships.
Requires explicit answer requirements and supporting labels.

failures.detection: Coverage checks find a required source fact absent.
failures.recovery: Rebuild context or use targeted extraction before answering.
Deduplicate by source version and preserve one authoritative copy.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming a large window guarantees comprehension
mistakes.fix: Test evidence use at different positions.

mistakes.mistake: Blindly putting all best passages at both ends
mistakes.fix: Measure ordering strategies and avoid unnecessary duplication.

whenToUse: Use for long prompts with known omission failures.
Use for agreement, policy, and multi-document synthesis.
Use when model upgrades change evidence-use behavior.
whenNotToUse: Avoid extra extraction stages for short reliable contexts.
Do not treat the effect as identical across all models.
Avoid ordering tricks as a substitute for relevant retrieval.
checklist: Hold evidence constant while testing placement.
Repeat tests after model and template changes.
